note: The main banks: AIB and Bank of Ireland, Ireland's two largest retail banks; PTSB, the third, refused an automated request (403) and isn't written. AIB's credit card rates (last reviewed 14 April 2025, still the page AIB publishes) and its credit cards page (read 2026-10-30): the CLICK Visa (9.11% a year), Platinum Visa (11.84%), 'be' Visa and Student Visa (14.85%; for third-level students, not checked). The 'be' Visa's rate is 14.16% a year when 5,000 euros or more is spent in 12 months, otherwise 16.79%: written as the range 14.16% to 16.79%. AIB charges no annual bank fee; the government's 30-euro annual stamp duty on each credit card account is written as each card's yearly fee. The Ascent Visa, on the rates page but not among the cards AIB offers, and the four cards AIB no longer opens aren't written. Bank of Ireland's credit cards page (read 2026-10-30): the Aer Credit Card (14% a year; 6.50 euros a month), Classic (16.12%), Platinum (13.79%; 76.18 euros a year), Affinity (14.57%) and Student (14.54%; for full-time students, with a limit of 600 to 1,000 euros, not written), each with the 30-euro stamp duty as a yearly fee. Neither bank's pages give a cash advance, foreign transaction, grace period or default fee for these cards (AIB's fees and charges page refused an automated request), so none is written; introductory offers aren't written. In wave 4 (2026-10-30) Avant Money, Ireland's largest card issuer outside the banks, was tried: its site answered with a Cloudflare check ('Just a moment', 403), not circumvented; PTSB's card page refused the request again (403); no bank was added. The minimum payment: AIB's personal credit card terms and conditions (effective 25 August 2025) let the holder choose it by direct debit as 3%, 5%, 10% or more of the balance, and set it at 3% of the balance or 6.35 euros, whichever is greater, for a holder who chooses none; written as 3% with a 6.35-euro floor for all four AIB cards (its 'be' card's standard information says the same). Bank of Ireland's distance contract information for personal credit cards (valid from June 2026): the balance if under 5 euros, otherwise the greater of 5 euros or 2.5% of the balance, written as 2.5% with a 5-euro floor for all five.
